app.title: Scratch2Arduino
app.welcome: Welcome to Scratch2Arduino! Plug in your Arduino board and start snapping blocks together.
app.coming_soon: The block editor is coming soon.

error.file_not_found: The file cannot be found. Was it moved or renamed?
error.read_failed: The file cannot be read. Check that you are allowed to open it.
error.write_failed: The file cannot be saved. Check that there is free space and that you can write to this folder.
error.invalid_archive: This file is not a Scratch2Arduino project (.s2a), or it is damaged.
error.invalid_json: The project content is damaged and cannot be read.
error.invalid_format: This file does not look like a Scratch2Arduino project.
error.unsupported_version: This project was made with a newer version of Scratch2Arduino. Update the software to open it.
error.invalid_catalog: The Scratch2Arduino block list is damaged. Reinstall the software.
error.process_failed: A tool needed by Scratch2Arduino could not be started. Reinstall the software.
error.unknown_board: This Arduino board is not supported (yet).
error.port_failed: The board's port cannot be used. Check the cable, and that no other program (serial monitor, Arduino IDE) is using the board.
error.board_not_responding: The board does not answer. Unplug it, plug it back in, then try again.
error.network_failed: The board cannot be reached over Wi-Fi. Check that the board is on and that the computer is on the same network (or on the board's own network "S2A-...", password scratch2arduino).

toolchain.platform_missing: The tools for this board are not installed yet. They will be downloaded (only once, Internet needed).
toolchain.library_missing: The program uses the "{library}" library, which is not installed.
toolchain.compiler_error: The program has {count} error(s). Check the highlighted blocks.
toolchain.sketch_too_big: The program is too big for this board's memory. Try to simplify it, or use a bigger board (Arduino Mega).
toolchain.not_enough_memory: The program uses too many variables for this board's memory. Try to remove some, or use a bigger board (Arduino Mega).
toolchain.port_not_found: The board cannot be found on port {port}. Check that it is plugged in, then choose the port again.
toolchain.port_busy: Port {port} is already used by another program (serial monitor, Arduino IDE...). Close it and try again.
toolchain.port_permission_denied: You are not allowed to use port {port}. On Linux, add your account to the "dialout" group (sudo usermod -aG dialout $USER), then log out and back in.
toolchain.board_not_responding: The board on {port} does not respond. Check that the right board is selected, try another USB cable, or press the board's RESET button.
toolchain.network_unavailable: The required tools cannot be downloaded. Check your Internet connection, then try again.
toolchain.timeout: The operation took too long and was stopped. Try again.
toolchain.unknown: Something unexpected went wrong. The technical details can help find the problem.

cli.usage:
Usage:
  s2a-cli boards                                 supported boards
  s2a-cli ports                                  plugged-in boards
  s2a-cli bluetooth                              Bluetooth boards around (ESP32), as bt:<address> ports
  s2a-cli setup [--board <id>]                   install the tools for a board (all by default)
  s2a-cli generate <project>                     print the Arduino code of a project (.s2a or project.json)
  s2a-cli wiring <project> [--svg <file>]        components to wire, their pins and the warnings (and the diagram)
  s2a-cli compile <folder|project> [--board <id>] compile an Arduino sketch or a project
  s2a-cli upload <folder|project> --port <port> [--board <id>]
  s2a-cli live <project> --port <port> [--seconds <n>]  run the blocks live (Ctrl+C stops)
  s2a-cli convert <file> --to cpp|python|javascript  rewrite a .ino/.cpp, .py or .js program in another language
  s2a-cli lib list|search <words>|install <name>[@<version>]|remove <name>  Arduino libraries (* = comes with a board)
  s2a-cli version
Options: --lang fr|en, --verbose
cli.convert_source: The file to convert must end with .ino, .cpp, .h, .py or .js.
cli.convert_check: Lines to convert by hand (kept as comments): {lines}.
cli.arduino_cli_missing: The arduino-cli tool cannot be found. Reinstall Scratch2Arduino.

cli.compiled: Compiled: the program uses {text} of {text_max} bytes ({text_percent}%), the variables {data} of {data_max} bytes.

cli.uploaded: The program has been sent to the board!

cli.live_running: Live mode: the blocks are running on the board. Ctrl+C to stop.
cli.bluetooth_none: No "S2A-..." Bluetooth board found. The board must have received the Live program once over USB.

validation.no_start_block: Your program does not start anywhere.
validation.no_start_block_hint: Add the "{block}" block (Events category) and attach your blocks below it.
validation.empty_script: The "{block}" block has nothing below it.
validation.empty_script_hint: Attach blocks below it to tell the board what to do.
validation.empty_mouth_hint: Put blocks inside it, otherwise it does nothing.
validation.blocks_after_forever: The "{block}" block comes after "forever": it will never run.
validation.blocks_after_forever_hint: Move it before the loop, or inside it if it should repeat.
validation.missing_condition: A condition is missing in the "{block}" block.
validation.missing_condition_hint: Drop a hexagonal block (for example "pin ... is HIGH" or "... > ...") into the empty slot.
validation.invalid_number: "{value}" is not a number, in the "{block}" block.
validation.invalid_number_hint: Type a number, for example 1 or 0.5.
validation.invalid_pin: Pin {pin} does not exist on the {board} board ("{block}" block).
validation.invalid_pin_hint: Click the pin number and pick one from the list.
validation.pin_capability: Pin {pin} of the {board} board cannot do "{capability}" ("{block}" block).
validation.missing_variable: No variable is chosen in the "{block}" block.
validation.missing_variable_hint: Make a variable (Variables category), then pick it in the block.
validation.unknown_block: This version of Scratch2Arduino does not know the "{block}" block.
validation.unknown_block_hint: Update Scratch2Arduino, or replace this block.
validation.missing_function: The "{block}" block uses no function, or a function that was deleted.
validation.missing_function_hint: Pick a function in its menu, or create one with "Create a function".
validation.function_not_defined: The "{function}" function is called, but no "define {function}" block says what it does.
validation.function_not_defined_hint: Drag a "define" block from the Functions category, pick "{function}" and attach blocks below it.
validation.function_defined_twice: The "{function}" function is defined twice: the program cannot tell which one to use.
validation.function_defined_twice_hint: Keep a single "define {function}" block: gather the blocks below it, or rename one of the functions.
validation.recursive_function: The "{function}" function ends up calling itself: it would never stop.
validation.recursive_function_hint: A function cannot call itself, not even through another function. Use "repeat" or "forever" instead.
validation.parameter_outside_function: The "{name}" block is the input of a function: it only works in the blocks of that function.
validation.parameter_outside_function_hint: Put it below the "define" block of the function that has the "{name}" input, or add this input to the function (right-click "define", then Edit the function).
validation.blocked: Problems to fix before your program can be sent: {count}.
validation.no_bluetooth: The {board} board has no Bluetooth: the "{block}" block cannot talk to the phone.
validation.no_bluetooth_hint: Choose an ESP32 board, or an Arduino board (Uno, Nano, Mega) with an HC-05 / HC-06 module, or remove the Phone blocks.
validation.module_missing: The {board} board has no Bluetooth: the "{block}" block needs an HC-05 / HC-06 module.
validation.module_missing_hint: Wire an HC-05 or HC-06 module and add the "Bluetooth module" block (Phone category) under "when the program starts".
validation.module_not_needed: The {board} board already has Bluetooth: the "{block}" block is not needed.
validation.module_not_needed_hint: Remove this block: the Phone blocks use the board's own Bluetooth.
validation.module_pins: The Bluetooth module cannot be on these pins: {problem}
validation.module_pins_hint: Choose other pins in the block, and wire the module the same way.
validation.module_twice: There are two "{block}" blocks with different pins: the module is wired in one place only.
validation.module_twice_hint: Keep a single "Bluetooth module" block, or give both the same pins.
validation.usercode_missing: "{name}" is not (or no longer) in "My code".
validation.usercode_missing_hint: Check its name in your code (capital letters matter), or remove this block.
validation.usercode_no_value: The function "{name}" gives no value: it cannot go in a slot.
validation.usercode_no_value_hint: Add a "return" with a value to your function, or use the block that runs it.
validation.usercode_read_only: "{name}" is a constant: a block cannot change it.
validation.usercode_read_only_hint: Remove "const" in your code if it must change.
validation.usercode_owned: "{name}" is changed by a function of "My code": blocks can read it, not change it (they would disturb your code).
validation.usercode_owned_hint: Change it in your code, or write in "My code" a function that changes it and call it with a block.

editor.no_port: Plug in your Arduino board, then pick its port before uploading.
editor.uploading: Sending the program to the board...
editor.code_note: This code is made from your blocks. Change the blocks to change it.
editor.unsaved_text: Your project has unsaved changes. Do you want to save them?

live.wiring_checking: Checking the wiring: reading the buttons and sensors...
live.wiring_button_pressed: The button on pin {pin} seems always pressed. It must be wired between pin {pin} and GND, with its legs on each side of the gap of the breadboard.
live.wiring_digital_floating: Pin {pin} changes value by itself: it seems to "float". Check its wire, add a resistor to GND, or use the block that sets the pin as an input with pull-up.
live.wiring_analog_floating: The values of pin {pin} jump around while nothing moves? Check the middle wire of the sensor and its wires to 5V and GND.
live.wiring_no_echo: The distance sensor (Trig {trig}, Echo {echo}) gets no echo. Check Trig and Echo (not swapped), VCC on 5V and GND, and that something is in front of it, closer than 4 m.
live.wiring_dht: The {model} sensor on pin {pin} does not answer. Check its data wire on pin {pin}, VCC and GND, and the model chosen in the block (DHT11 or DHT22).
live.flashing: Installing the Live program on the {board} board (only once, a few seconds)...
live.running: Live mode: your blocks are running on the board. Change them and the board follows!
live.finished: Every block has run. Change them to start again.
live.wifi_no_firmware: The board does not answer over Wi-Fi. Plug it in once with the USB cable and start the Live mode: the Live program is installed on it, with Wi-Fi.
live.wifi_joined: The board joined the "{network}" network: its address is {address}.
live.wifi_not_joined: The board cannot join the "{network}" network. Check the name and the password (capital letters matter). It can still be reached on its own network "{access_point}".
live.wifi_forgotten: The board forgot the home network: it can still be reached on its own network "{access_point}".
live.wifi_upload: A program is sent with the USB cable: choose the board's USB port (Wi-Fi and Bluetooth are for the Live mode).
live.wifi_monitor: The serial monitor uses the USB cable: choose the board's USB port. In Live mode over Wi-Fi or Bluetooth, what the blocks write is shown in the Live panel.
live.sim_upload: The virtual board takes no program: click Live to run your blocks on it, or choose the USB port of a real board to send it.
live.sim_monitor: The virtual board has no serial monitor: in Live mode, what the blocks write is shown in the Live panel.
live.bluetooth_no_firmware: The board does not answer over Bluetooth. Check that it is switched on and near the computer. The first time, plug it in with the USB cable and start the Live mode: the Live program is installed on it, with Bluetooth.
live.bluetooth_off: Bluetooth boards cannot be searched for: the computer's Bluetooth may be off. Switch it on, then try again.
live.phone_bluetooth: The Phone blocks need the board's Bluetooth for the phone: start the Live mode over the USB cable or Wi-Fi.
live.module_pins: Pins {rx} and {tx} are used by the Bluetooth module (HC-05 / HC-06): the highlighted blocks must use other pins, or the module must be wired to other pins (Bluetooth button).

wiring.pin_twice: Pin {pin} is used by both "{first}" and "{second}": each component needs its own pin.
wiring.i2c_taken: Pin {pin} carries the I2C of "{screen}": "{other}" must use another pin.
wiring.power: The components need about {current} mA, more than the 500 mA of a USB port: power the board with a mains adapter, and the motors or the LED strip with their own supply (GNDs joined).

text.unknown_name: "{name}" is unknown: check the spelling (capital letters matter) and that it is declared before it is used.
text.missing_semicolon: A ";" is missing at the end of an instruction (often on the line before).
text.missing_closing: A "{symbol}" is missing: every opened bracket or brace must be closed.
text.unknown_member: "{object}" has no function or field "{name}": check the spelling.
text.cpp_empty: The program is empty: write at least the setup() and loop() functions.
text.cpp_missing_function: The {name}() function is missing: an Arduino program always has void setup() { ... } and void loop() { ... }.
text.cpp_library_missing: The program uses the "{library}" library, which is not installed. Open the Libraries window to find it and add it to the project.
text.script_upload: A Python or JavaScript program runs on the computer and drives the board: use the Live button instead of Upload.
text.script_ok: Well done, your program can be read! Start it with the Live button.
text.pin_unknown: Pin {pin} does not exist on the {board} board.
text.pin_mode_unknown: pinMode expects OUTPUT, INPUT or INPUT_PULLUP.
text.pin_not_analog: analogRead needs an analog pin (A0, A1...): pin {pin} is not one.
text.pin_not_pwm: analogWrite needs a PWM pin (marked ~ on the board): pin {pin} is not one.
text.pin_expected: A pin is needed: a number (13) or a name ("A0").
text.argument_count: This function did not get the right number of values between its brackets.
text.not_a_script: This program is not written in Python or JavaScript.
text.python_indentation: The indentation is wrong: the lines of a block must start at the same distance from the edge, and the line after a ":" must be indented.
text.python_syntax: Python does not understand this line: check the brackets, the quotes and the ":" at the end of if, while, for and def. ({message})
text.javascript_syntax: JavaScript does not understand this line: check the brackets, the braces and the quotes. ({message})
text.division_by_zero: Division by zero: nothing can be divided by 0.
text.live_cpp: A C++ program is sent to the board with Upload. Live mode is for blocks, Python and JavaScript.
text.running: Your program runs on the computer and drives the board. The Stop button stops it.
text.usercode_convert_lines: "My code" is written in {language}: to upload it, it is translated to C++, but these lines could not be: {lines}. Simplify them, write "My code" in C++, or use the Live button.
text.usercode_convert_line: This line could not be translated to C++ for the board.
text.usercode_upload_only: Your blocks use "My code" written in C++: it is compiled for the board, send the program with Upload (or write "My code" in Python or JavaScript for the Live mode).

module.usb: The module's pins are saved on the board with the USB cable: plug the board in and choose its USB port.
module.no_module: This board does not take an HC-05 / HC-06 module: its Bluetooth is built in.
module.pins_usb: Pins 0 and 1 carry the USB link: wire the module to other pins (10 and 11 for example).
module.pins_same: The module needs two different pins: one that receives (wired to TXD) and one that sends (wired to RXD).
module.pin_missing: This board has no such digital pin: choose pins written on the board.
module.pin_receive: On a Mega, the pin that receives must be 10, 11, 12, 13, 50, 51, 52, 53 or A8 to A15, or use a serial port of the board: 19 and 18, 17 and 16, or 15 and 14.
module.speed: This speed is not one of the module's: use 9600 (the speed of a new module), 19200, 38400, 57600 or 115200.
module.saved: Saved on the board: the module is on pins {rx} (to TXD) and {tx} (to RXD), at {baud} baud. Now pair the module with the computer, then search for it.
module.saved_restart: Saved on the board: pins {rx} (to TXD) and {tx} (to RXD), at {baud} baud. Press the board's reset button (or unplug it and plug it in again) so that it uses them.
module.forgotten: The board forgot the module: its pins are free again after the next start of the board.
